candidates.test_case: Measure luminous intensities of random production lamps on a goniophotometer, with the LED light sources present, at the test voltage, and check deviations against the 20 per cent limit.
candidates.applies_because: Each R148 lamp function of the product is subject to conformity of production photometric checks.

candidates.text: For required minimum values throughout the fields specified in Annexes 2 and 3, the measured values of production lamps shall be at least the 20 per cent equivalents in Table 12: 0.7 cd → 0.5 cd; 0.6 cd → 0.4 cd; 0.3 cd → 0.2 cd; 0.07 cd → 0.05 cd; 0.05 cd → 0.03 cd.
candidates.test_case: Measure intensities at the relevant grid and visibility points of production lamps and compare them with the Table 12 equivalent values.
candidates.applies_because: These small minimum values occur in the light distribution and geometric visibility fields of the rear position, stop and reversing lamps.

candidates.text: The chromaticity coordinates of mass-produced lamps shall comply with the requirements: red for the rear position and stop lamps, white for the reversing lamp. Compliance is checked when tested under the conditions of paragraph 4.9.
candidates.test_case: Measure chromaticity coordinates of random production lamps within the light distribution field using a spectroradiometer, with the light sources present.
candidates.applies_because: The colour of the light emitted by the red and white functions of the product must stay within limits in series production.

candidates.text: For the reversing lamp (AR) using LED light source technology, the luminous intensities measured after 1 minute of operation shall comply with the minimum and maximum requirements.
candidates.test_case: Operate the reversing lamp from cold at test voltage and measure the luminous intensity distribution after 1 minute (measured, or calculated via the HV ratio), then compare with the AR min/max values.
candidates.applies_because: The reversing lamp function uses non-incandescent (LED) light sources.

candidates.text: For the reversing lamp (AR) using LED light source technology, the luminous intensities measured after 10 minutes of operation shall comply with the minimum and maximum requirements.
candidates.test_case: Measure the reversing lamp luminous intensity distribution after 10 minutes of continuous operation (measured, or calculated via the HV ratio) and check it against the AR min/max values.
candidates.applies_because: The reversing lamp function uses non-incandescent (LED) light sources.

candidates.text: For the rear position lamp (R1/R2) and the stop lamp (S1/S2) using LED light source technology, the luminous intensities measured after 1 minute of operation shall comply with the minimum and maximum requirements.
candidates.test_case: Switch on each function from cold and measure the intensity distribution after 1 minute (or calculate it via the HV ratio), then compare with the Table 4/Table 7 min/max values.
candidates.applies_because: The rear position and stop lamp functions use LED light sources and are not reversing or manoeuvring lamps.

candidates.text: For the rear position lamp (R1/R2) and the stop lamp (S1/S2) using LED light source technology, the luminous intensities measured either after 30 minutes of operation or after photometric stability has occurred shall comply with the minimum and maximum requirements.
candidates.test_case: Measure the full intensity distribution of each function after 30 minutes of operation, or once photometric stability is reached, and check it against the min/max values.
candidates.applies_because: The rear position and stop lamp functions use LED light sources and are not reversing or manoeuvring lamps.

candidates.text: Depending on the light source technology, the luminous intensity distribution of each lamp function shall, in addition to Annex 8 paragraph 1, comply at the point in time after switch-on listed in Table A8-1, evaluated at the reference coordinate given there.
candidates.test_case: Record the intensity at the reference coordinate at the specified time after switch-on and scale the paragraph 1 distribution by the ratio to verify compliance.
candidates.applies_because: The lamp includes rear position, stop and reversing functions listed in Table A8-1.

candidates.text: Points in time for additional testing: front and rear position lamp, 4 s after switch ON, reference coordinate HV; stop lamp, 0.2 s after switch ON, reference coordinate HV; reversing lamp, 0.2 s after switch ON, reference coordinate HV.
candidates.test_case: Use a fast photometer at HV to capture intensity at 4 s (rear position) and 0.2 s (stop, reversing) after switch-on.
candidates.applies_because: These rows cover the rear position, stop and reversing functions of the product.

candidates.text: Where a lamp function uses LED technology only, the lamp function is deemed to comply with the intensity requirements at all points in time if the values measured according to Annex 8 paragraph 1.2 are compliant.
candidates.test_case: Confirm from the design documentation that each function is LED-only and that the paragraph 1.2 measurements pass.
candidates.applies_because: All three lamp functions use non-replaceable LED light sources only.

candidates.text: In case of doubt (e.g. unexpected run-up behaviour), the minimum intensity requirements of each lamp function shall be met at all points in time, starting at the point in time listed in Table A8-1 (rear position 4 s; stop and reversing 0.2 s) and ending when photometric stability is reached.
candidates.test_case: Continuously record intensity at HV from the Table A8-1 start time until stabilization and verify it never falls below the minimum.
candidates.applies_because: LED driver electronics may cause unexpected run-up behaviour in the product's functions.

candidates.text: Every retro-reflector belonging to an approved type shall comprise a space of sufficient size for either the Unique Identifier and the other markings defined in paragraph 3.3.4.2, or the approval marking and the other markings defined in paragraph 3.3.4.2.
candidates.test_case: Inspect the drawing and a sample to confirm a marking area large enough for the approval mark or UI plus the trade name and any 'TOP' marking.
candidates.applies_because: The integral red retro-reflector (P-05) is a retro-reflective device approved under R150 and must carry its marking.

candidates.text: All markings on the retro-reflector shall be clearly legible and indelible.
candidates.test_case: Visually check legibility and perform a rub/durability check of the moulded or printed markings.
candidates.applies_because: The R150 markings for the retro-reflector are placed on the product.

candidates.text: The size of the approval marking shall be based on the value of 'a' defined in Table 1.
candidates.test_case: Measure the approval mark dimensions on the tool drawing and a production part.
candidates.applies_because: The approval marking for the Class IA/IB retro-reflector must respect the minimum dimension 'a'.

candidates.text: For a retro-reflector for motor vehicles, the identifying symbol and minimum 'a' are: Class IA (independent) – symbol 'IA', minimum 'a' = 5 mm; Class IB (combined with other signal lamps which are not watertight) – symbol 'IB', minimum 'a' = 5 mm.
candidates.test_case: Check that the marked class symbol matches the approved class and that 'a' is at least 5 mm.
candidates.applies_because: The product's retro-reflector is Class IA if the lamp is watertight and Class IB if it is not.

candidates.text: If the approval marking is used, it shall include the approval mark, i.e. a circle surrounding the letter 'E' followed by the distinguishing number of the country which has granted approval.
candidates.test_case: Inspect the marking for a circle enclosing 'E' and the country number.
candidates.applies_because: The retro-reflector must bear the approval marking unless the Unique Identifier is used.

candidates.text: If the approval marking is used, it shall include the four- to six-digit sequential number that forms part of the approval number.
candidates.test_case: Inspect the marking for the 4- to 6-digit sequential number from the approval.
candidates.applies_because: This is part of the approval marking content for the retro-reflector.

candidates.text: The sequential number shall be placed close to the approval mark.
candidates.test_case: Visually verify that the sequential number is adjacent to the E-circle.
candidates.applies_because: This governs the layout of the retro-reflector approval marking.

candidates.text: If the approval marking is used, it shall include the symbol identifying the retro-reflective device: in case of a watertight lamp (independent retro-reflector, Class IA), the symbol 'IA'; in case of a lamp that is not watertight (Class IB), the symbol 'IB'.
candidates.test_case: Compare the marked class symbol with the class in the approval documentation.
candidates.applies_because: The class symbol depends on the open option for housing watertightness.

candidates.text: If the approval marking is used, it shall include the number of this Regulation followed by the letter 'R' and the two digits indicating the series of amendments in force at the time of issue of the approval (e.g. '150R01').
candidates.test_case: Inspect the marking for the '150R' code and the correct series digits.
candidates.applies_because: This is part of the approval marking content for the retro-reflector.

candidates.text: In case the approval marking is replaced by the Unique Identifier, the UI mark shall follow the format shown in Figure I of the Regulation.
candidates.test_case: Compare the UI marking on the part with the Figure I format.
candidates.applies_because: The manufacturer may use the UI instead of the approval marking on the retro-reflector.

candidates.text: The retro-reflector shall bear the trade name or mark of the applicant.
candidates.test_case: Visually inspect the part for the applicant's trade name or mark.
candidates.applies_because: This is a mandatory marking on every R150 retro-reflective device.

candidates.text: For a Class IA or IB retro-reflector, the word 'TOP' shall be inscribed horizontally on the highest part of the illuminating surface if such an indication is necessary to determine without ambiguity the angle or angles of rotation prescribed by the manufacturer.
candidates.test_case: Assess whether the rotation angle is ambiguous and, if so, verify that 'TOP' is present horizontally at the highest part of the illuminating surface.
candidates.applies_because: The retro-reflector is non-triangular Class IA/IB and may need an orientation indication.

candidates.text: The approval marking or the Unique Identifier, and the markings of paragraph 3.3.4, shall be clearly legible on the retro-reflective device.
candidates.test_case: Visually verify legibility of all markings on the assembled device.
candidates.applies_because: This sets the marking location requirement for the retro-reflector.

candidates.text: In case a single approval mark (with sequential number or UI) is affixed to the combined rear lamp covering several UN Regulations, the mark shall be visible after installation of the lamp on the vehicle.
candidates.test_case: Install the lamp in the vehicle or a representative fixture and check that the single approval mark is visible.
candidates.applies_because: The retro-reflector is combined with R148 lamps, and a single grouped mark may be used.

candidates.text: In case a single approval mark is used, no part of the combined lamp that transmits light shall be removable without at the same time removing the approval mark with the sequential number or the Unique Identifier.
candidates.test_case: Review the design to confirm that removing any light-transmitting part (lens, retro-reflector) also removes the mark-bearing part.
candidates.applies_because: The combined rear lamp has light-transmitting parts (outer lens, retro-reflector insert) that the mark must be tied to.

candidates.text: In case a single approval mark is used for the combined lamp, the size of its components shall not be less than the minimum size required for the smallest of the individual marks by the pertinent UN Regulations under which approval has been granted.
candidates.test_case: Measure the single mark components and compare them with the minimum sizes required by R150 and R148.
candidates.applies_because: This applies to a grouped mark covering R150 (retro-reflector) and R148 (lamp functions).

candidates.text: Retro-reflectors approved under this Regulation shall be so manufactured as to conform to the approved type by meeting the requirements set forth in paragraphs 4 and 5.
candidates.test_case: Perform periodic CoP photometric, colorimetric and water-penetration tests on production parts.
candidates.applies_because: Production retro-reflectors of the rear lamp must match the approved type.

candidates.text: When the photometric performance of any production retro-reflector chosen at random is tested, no measured value shall deviate unfavourably by more than 20 per cent from the minimum values prescribed in this Regulation.
candidates.test_case: Measure the RI of random production samples and confirm that each value is at least 80% of the Table 3 minima.
candidates.applies_because: This is the CoP photometric tolerance for production retro-reflectors referenced by paragraph 3.5.1.1.

candidates.text: Production retro-reflectors shall comply with the chromaticity coordinates prescribed for red.
candidates.test_case: Measure the night-time trichromatic coordinates of production samples against the R48 red limits.
candidates.applies_because: This CoP colour requirement applies to the red retro-reflector.

candidates.text: The requirements of sections 5 (General specifications) and 6 (Individual specifications) of UN Regulation No. 48, and the annexes referenced there, in the series of amendments in force at the time of application, that are pertinent to the rear retro-reflector and to category M1 vehicles shall apply to the retro-reflector wherever they can be verified at retro-reflector type approval.
candidates.test_case: Review the R48 sections 5 and 6 provisions applicable to rear retro-reflectors on M1 and verify the device-level ones (e.g. shape, colour, visibility-related design) at approval.
candidates.applies_because: The red rear retro-reflector is intended for installation on M1 vehicles governed by R48.

candidates.text: The retro-reflector shall be so constructed that it functions satisfactorily and will continue to do so in normal use.
candidates.test_case: Verify by passing the prescribed photometric, colorimetric and resistance tests (heat, water/dust, corrosion, fuel/oil).
candidates.applies_because: The integral red retro-reflector (P-05) is a retro-reflective device under R150.

candidates.text: The retro-reflector shall not have any defect in design or manufacture that is detrimental to its efficient operation or to its maintenance in good condition.
candidates.test_case: Visually inspect the samples for design or moulding defects (sink marks, damaged prisms, voids) before and after the tests.
candidates.applies_because: The integral red retro-reflector (P-05) is a retro-reflective device under R150.

candidates.text: The components of the retro-reflector or parts thereof shall not be capable of being easily dismantled.
candidates.test_case: Attempt manual disassembly of the retro-reflector components without tools and confirm they cannot be easily separated.
candidates.applies_because: The retro-reflector insert is built into the lamp between lens and gasket and must not be easily removable.

candidates.text: The outer surface of the retro-reflector shall be easy to clean.
candidates.test_case: Inspect the outer surface and carry out a cleaning trial to confirm dirt can be easily removed.
candidates.applies_because: The outer surface of the retro-reflector (or of the lamp lens covering it) is exposed on the vehicle rear.

candidates.text: The outer surface of the retro-reflector shall not be rough.
candidates.test_case: Visual/tactile inspection or surface roughness measurement of the outer surface.
candidates.applies_because: The outer surface of the retro-reflector is exposed on the vehicle rear.

candidates.text: Any protuberances on the outer surface of the retro-reflector shall not prevent easy cleaning.
candidates.test_case: Inspect the outer surface geometry for protuberances that would trap dirt or hinder wiping.
candidates.applies_because: The outer surface of the retro-reflector is exposed on the vehicle rear.

candidates.text: There shall be no access to the inner surface of the retro-reflector when in normal use.
candidates.test_case: Inspect the assembled lamp to confirm the retro-reflector's inner (prism) surface cannot be reached without dismantling.
candidates.applies_because: The prism (inner) surface of the integral retro-reflector must be enclosed within the lamp.

candidates.text: In case the retro-reflector consists of a colourless retro-reflecting optical unit combined with a filter (e.g. the red outer lens), the optical unit and the filter shall be so designed that they cannot be separated under normal conditions of use.
candidates.test_case: Inspect the assembly and attempt separation of the optical unit and filter under normal-use handling to confirm they stay joined.
candidates.applies_because: An open option is that the retro-reflector is a colourless optical unit behind the red outer lens acting as filter.

candidates.text: The retro-reflecting optical unit and any filter shall not be coloured by means of paint or varnish.
candidates.test_case: Check the material specification and inspect/section the optical unit and filter to confirm the colour is in the material, not a paint or varnish layer.
candidates.applies_because: The retro-reflector must be red, by coloured PMMA or a red filter, not by paint or varnish.

candidates.text: When illuminated by CIE Standard Illuminant A with an angle of divergence of 1/3° and an illumination angle β1 = β2 = 0° (or β1 = -5°, β2 = 0° if a colourless surface reflection occurs), the trichromatic coordinates of the luminous intensity reflected by the retro-reflector shall be within the limits for the red night-time colour of retro-reflected light defined in UN Regulation No. 48.
candidates.test_case: Measure the chromaticity of the retro-reflected light with Illuminant A at 1/3° divergence and 0°/0° (or -5°/0°) and compare with the R48 red night-time limits.
candidates.applies_because: The retro-reflector is a red retro-reflective device, to which the night-time colour specifications apply.

candidates.text: Every red retro-reflector of Class IA or IB, when tested according to paragraph 5.1.7, shall meet the dimension and shape requirements of Annex 5.
candidates.test_case: Visually inspect the shape and measure the dimensions of the retro-reflector against Annex 5, paragraph 1.
candidates.applies_because: The integral red non-triangular retro-reflector (P-05) is approved as Class IA or IB under R150.

candidates.text: Every retro-reflector of Class IA or IB, when tested according to paragraph 5.1.7, shall meet the photometric and colorimetric requirements of paragraphs 5.1.4 to 5.1.5.
candidates.test_case: Perform RI photometry and night-time colorimetry on the samples per paragraphs 5.1.4 and 5.1.5.
candidates.applies_because: P-05 is a Class IA/IB retro-reflector.

candidates.text: Every retro-reflector of Class IA or IB shall meet the physical and mechanical requirements of paragraph 5.1.7, depending on the nature of its materials and construction.
candidates.test_case: Run the heat, water, fuel, oil, corrosion, rear-face, stability and weathering tests in the Table 4 sequence and check the results.
candidates.applies_because: P-05 is a moulded PMMA Class IA/IB retro-reflector subject to the resistance tests.

candidates.text: The shape of the illuminating surfaces of a Class IA or IB retro-reflector shall not be easily confused with the triangular shape prescribed for trailer retro-reflectors, when viewed from an observation distance of 10 m.
candidates.test_case: Visually inspect the retro-reflector from 10 m and confirm it cannot be confused with a triangle.
candidates.applies_because: P-05 is a non-triangular Class IA/IB retro-reflector.

candidates.text: The moulded plastics retro-reflector of Class IA or IB shall withstand being kept for 48 consecutive hours in a dry atmosphere at 65 °C ± 2 °C, followed by cooling for 1 hour at 23 °C ± 2 °C.
candidates.test_case: Condition the samples for 48 h at 65 °C in dry air, cool them for 1 h at 23 °C, then inspect them.
candidates.applies_because: P-05 is a moulded PMMA reflector of Class IA/IB.

candidates.text: After the heat resistance test, no cracking or appreciable distortion of the retro-reflector, and in particular of its optical component, shall be visible.
candidates.test_case: Visually inspect the samples after the heat test for cracks or distortion of the optics.
candidates.applies_because: This is the heat test pass criterion for the Class IA/IB retro-reflector.

candidates.text: At least one hour after the heat resistance test, the retro-reflector shall meet the colorimetric requirements of paragraph 5.1.5 and the RI requirements of paragraph 5.1.4 for an angle of divergence of 20' and an illumination angle β1 = β2 = 0° (or, if necessary, the position defined in Annex 4 Part 1, paragraphs 1.1 and 1.2).
candidates.test_case: Measure the colour and RI at 20', β1=β2=0° on all samples at least 1 h after the heat test.
candidates.applies_because: The heat-conditioned retro-reflector samples must still meet the colour and RI limits.

candidates.text: After the heat resistance test, the retro-reflector samples giving the minimum and maximum RI values shall meet the complete photometric requirements of paragraph 5.1.4.
candidates.test_case: Perform complete photometry over all Table 3 angles on the minimum and maximum RI samples.
candidates.applies_because: The full photometry of the Class IA/IB device is verified on the extreme samples.

candidates.text: The retro-reflector, as part of the lamp and stripped of all removable parts, shall withstand immersion for 10 minutes in water at 50 °C ± 5 °C. The highest point of the illuminating surface shall be 20 mm below the water surface, and the immersion is repeated in the inverted position. The retro-reflector shall then withstand immediate immersion under the same conditions in water at 25 °C ± 5 °C.
candidates.test_case: Immerse the lamp or retro-reflector at 50 °C in the normal and then the inverted position, then at 25 °C, and inspect it.
candidates.applies_because: The Class IA/IB retro-reflector built into the lamp undergoes the water penetration test.

candidates.text: After the water penetration test, no water shall penetrate to the reflecting surface of the retro-reflecting optical unit.
candidates.test_case: Visually inspect the prism reflecting surface for water after immersion, and measure the RI in case of doubt.
candidates.applies_because: This is the water test pass criterion for the Class IA/IB retro-reflector, which depends on the lens, gasket and housing sealing.

candidates.text: If visual inspection does not reveal water after the water penetration test, or in case of doubt, the RI of the retro-reflector, measured as in paragraph 5.1.3.2.2 after lightly shaking off excess water, shall meet the requirements of paragraph 5.1.4.
candidates.test_case: Shake off excess water and measure the RI at 20', β1=β2=0°.
candidates.applies_because: The RI must be confirmed on the retro-reflector after the water test.

candidates.text: After the water penetration test followed by the tests for resistance to fuels and lubricating oils, the retro-reflector shall have a colour which satisfies paragraph 5.1.5.
candidates.test_case: Check the colour visually, and the trichromatic coordinates in case of doubt, after the water, fuel and oil tests.
candidates.applies_because: The PMMA retro-reflector is exposed to fuels and oils in the first test group.

candidates.text: After the water penetration test followed by the tests for resistance to fuels and lubricating oils, the retro-reflector shall have an RI which satisfies paragraph 5.1.4, verified at an angle of divergence of 20' and illumination angle β1 = β2 = 0° (or, if necessary, all positions in Annex 4 Part 1, paragraphs 1.1 and 1.2).
candidates.test_case: Measure the RI at 20', β1=β2=0° after the water, fuel and oil tests.
candidates.applies_because: This is the pass criterion for the first test group of the Class IA/IB retro-reflector.

candidates.text: In case the retro-reflector has essential metal components susceptible to corrosion and/or an accessible mirror-backed rear face, after the corrosion test and/or the rear-face abrasion test the retro-reflector shall have a colour which satisfies paragraph 5.1.5.
candidates.test_case: Check the colour after the corrosion and rear-face brushing tests where applicable.
candidates.applies_because: The open options include metal components and a mirror-backed rear face on P-05.

candidates.text: In case the retro-reflector has essential metal components susceptible to corrosion and/or an accessible mirror-backed rear face, after the corrosion test and/or the rear-face abrasion test the retro-reflector shall have an RI which satisfies paragraph 5.1.4, verified at 20' divergence and β1 = β2 = 0°.
candidates.test_case: Measure the RI at 20', β1=β2=0° after the corrosion and rear-face tests where applicable.
candidates.applies_because: The open options include metal components and a mirror-backed rear face on P-05.

candidates.text: After the test for stability in time of the optical properties (Annex 4 Part 3), the retro-reflector shall have a colour which satisfies paragraph 5.1.5.
candidates.test_case: Check the colour after the stability-in-time test.
candidates.applies_because: The third test group applies to Class IA/IB retro-reflectors.

candidates.text: After the test for stability in time of the optical properties (Annex 4 Part 3), the retro-reflector shall have an RI which satisfies paragraph 5.1.4, verified at 20' divergence and β1 = β2 = 0°.
candidates.test_case: Measure the RI at 20', β1=β2=0° after the stability-in-time test.
candidates.applies_because: The third test group applies to Class IA/IB retro-reflectors.

candidates.text: After the resistance to weathering test (Annex 6 Part 6), the retro-reflector shall have a colour which satisfies paragraph 5.1.5.
candidates.test_case: Check the colour after accelerated weathering per EN ISO 4892-2.
candidates.applies_because: The fourth test group applies to Class IA/IB retro-reflectors.

candidates.text: After the resistance to weathering test (Annex 6 Part 6), the retro-reflector shall have an RI which satisfies paragraph 5.1.4, verified at 20' divergence and β1 = β2 = 0°.
candidates.test_case: Measure the RI at 20', β1=β2=0° after the weathering exposure.
candidates.applies_because: The fourth test group applies to Class IA/IB retro-reflectors.

candidates.text: Where more than one axis of reference, or a range of axes, is specified by the manufacturer, the retro-reflector shall meet the RI requirements with reference to each specified axis of reference or to the extreme axes of the specified range.
candidates.test_case: Repeat the photometric measurements for each declared axis of reference or for the extreme axes of the range.
candidates.applies_because: The axis of reference of P-05 is declared by the manufacturer and the photometry is referenced to it.

candidates.text: For photometric measurements of a Class IA or IB retro-reflector, only the illuminating surface defined by the planes contiguous to the outermost parts of the optical system, as indicated by the manufacturer, and contained within a circle of 200 mm diameter shall be considered.
candidates.test_case: Verify the declared illuminating surface lies within a 200 mm circle and mask the surrounding area during photometry.
candidates.applies_because: This defines the measured surface of the Class IA/IB retro-reflector.

candidates.text: The illuminating surface considered for photometry of a Class IA or IB retro-reflector shall be limited to 100 cm²; the retro-reflecting optical units need not attain this area.
candidates.test_case: Check on the drawing and sample that the illuminating surface used for photometry is no more than 100 cm².
candidates.applies_because: This limits the measured area of P-05.

candidates.text: The manufacturer shall specify the perimeter of the illuminating surface area of the retro-reflector to be used for photometric measurements.
candidates.test_case: Check that the drawing defines the perimeter of the illuminating surface.
candidates.applies_because: The design documentation of P-05 must define the photometric area.

candidates.text: When measured as described in Annex 4 Part 1, paragraph 3, the RI values of the red Class IA/IB retro-reflector shall be equal to or greater than the values in Table 3, in mcd/lx, for the angles of divergence and illumination shown.
candidates.test_case: Measure the RI with a goniometer at each Table 3 divergence and illumination angle and compare it with the minima.
candidates.applies_because: P-05 is a red Class IA/IB retro-reflector.

candidates.text: Minimum RI for a red Class IA/IB retro-reflector at divergence angle 20': 300 mcd/lx at β1=0°, β2=0°; 200 mcd/lx at β1=±10°, β2=0°; 100 mcd/lx at β1=±5°, β2=±20°. At divergence angle 1°30': 5 mcd/lx at β1=0°, β2=0°; 2.8 mcd/lx at β1=±10°, β2=0°; 2.5 mcd/lx at β1=±5°, β2=±20°.
candidates.test_case: Measure the RI at the six angle combinations and verify each is at or above the tabulated minimum.
candidates.applies_because: These are the Table 3 values for the red IA/IB class of P-05.

candidates.text: Within the solid angle having the centre of reference as its apex and bounded by the planes intersecting along the lines (β1 = ±10°, β2 = 0°) and (β1 = ±5°, β2 = ±20°), the RI values of the retro-reflector shall not be lower than those shown in the last two (applicable) columns of Table 3 for red Class IA/IB.
candidates.test_case: Scan the RI over the bounded solid angle and confirm no value falls below the applicable Table 3 minimum.
candidates.applies_because: This is an additional RI floor within the angular field of the Class IA/IB retro-reflector.

candidates.text: In case the Class IA or IB retro-reflector is intended to be installed with its H plane at a mounting height less than 750 mm above the ground, the RI values need be met only up to an angle of 5° downwards.
candidates.test_case: Check the declared mounting height and, if below 750 mm, limit the downward RI verification to 5°.
candidates.applies_because: The mounting height of the rear lamp on the M1 vehicle may be below 750 mm.

candidates.text: If the retro-reflector is not marked 'TOP', the RI at an illumination angle β1 = β2 = 0° and divergence 20' shall meet the paragraph 5 value with the device rotated about its axis of reference to the position of minimum RI.
candidates.test_case: Rotate the device about its axis of reference to the minimum-RI position and verify the 20', 0° value.
candidates.applies_because: This defines the orientation in which the RI of P-05 must comply.

candidates.text: The night-time colour of the retro-reflector shall be tested according to paragraph 4.2.1: illumination by CIE Standard Illuminant A at an angle of divergence of 1/3° and an illumination angle β1 = β2 = 0°, or the Annex 4 Part 1, paragraph 1.1 angle if 0° produces a colourless surface reflection.
candidates.test_case: Measure the chromaticity of the retro-reflected light under Illuminant A at 1/3° divergence.
candidates.applies_because: This defines the colour measurement conditions for the red retro-reflector.

candidates.text: The trichromatic coordinates of the luminous flux reflected by the retro-reflector shall be within the limits for the night-time colour red specified in UN Regulation No. 48.
candidates.test_case: Measure the x,y chromaticity of the reflected light with a spectroradiometer and compare it with the R48 red night-time boundaries.
candidates.applies_because: P-05 is a red rear retro-reflector, whether coloured itself or behind the red outer lens acting as filter.

candidates.text: Mass-produced retro-reflectors (Class IA/IB, red) shall not differ mechanically or geometrically from the approved type by more than inevitable manufacturing deviations within the requirements of this Regulation.
candidates.test_case: Measure shape and dimensions of random production retro-reflectors and compare with the approved drawings and the Annex 5 Class IA/IB requirements.
candidates.applies_because: The integral rear retro-reflector is approved under R150 and its series production must conform to the approved type.

candidates.text: When the photometric performance of any randomly chosen mass-produced retro-reflector is tested, no measured coefficient of luminous intensity value shall deviate unfavourably by more than 20 per cent from the minimum values prescribed in this Regulation.
candidates.test_case: Measure the CIL of random production samples at the prescribed observation and entrance angles and check each value is at least 80 per cent of the prescribed minimum.
candidates.applies_because: The production retro-reflector of the rear lamp must keep its CIL within this conformity-of-production tolerance.

candidates.text: Mass-produced retro-reflectors shall comply with the chromaticity coordinates prescribed for red retro-reflected light.
candidates.test_case: Measure the chromaticity coordinates of the retro-reflected light of random production samples and check they lie within the red boundaries of the Regulation.
candidates.applies_because: The rear retro-reflector is red, and its production colour must stay within the red chromaticity limits.

candidates.text: Mass-produced retro-reflectors (Class IA/IB) shall conform to the approved type mechanically and geometrically, with differences not exceeding inevitable manufacturing deviations.
candidates.test_case: Measure the shape and dimensions of production retro-reflectors and compare them with the approved drawings and Annex 5 Class IA/IB requirements.
candidates.applies_because: The integral red retro-reflector of the rear lamp is approved under R150 and its series production must match the approved type.

candidates.text: When the photometric performance of any randomly chosen mass-produced retro-reflector is tested, no measured value shall deviate unfavourably by more than 20 per cent from the minimum values prescribed in this Regulation.
candidates.test_case: Measure the CIL of randomly selected production retro-reflectors at all prescribed angles and check that every value is at least 80 per cent of the prescribed minimum.
candidates.applies_because: This limits how far the photometric performance (CIL) of a production unit of the lamp's retro-reflector may deviate.

candidates.text: Mass-produced retro-reflectors shall comply with the prescribed chromaticity coordinates (red).
candidates.test_case: Measure the chromaticity coordinates of production retro-reflectors under the prescribed colorimetric conditions and check that they lie within the red boundaries.
candidates.applies_because: The red retro-reflector, including any red outer lens acting as a filter, must keep its colour within the red limits in series production.

candidates.text: Mass-produced retro-reflectors shall pass the resistance to water penetration test of paragraph 1 of Part 2 of Annex 6, with no water penetrating to the reflecting surface of the retro-reflecting optical unit.
candidates.test_case: Immerse a production retro-reflector in water at 50 °C and then at 25 °C per Annex 6 Part 2, then inspect it visually for water and re-measure the CIL if in doubt.
candidates.applies_because: Production units of the lamp's retro-reflector, whether part of a lamp or not, are subject to the water penetration check during conformity of production.

candidates.text: When the RI of the retro-reflector is measured at β1 = β2 = 0° and a mirror effect is produced, the RI shall be assessed with an illumination angle of β1 = -5°, β2 = 0°.
candidates.test_case: Turn the device slightly at β1 = β2 = 0° to check for a mirror effect; if one is present, measure RI at β1 = -5°, β2 = 0° and compare with Table 3.
candidates.applies_because: This angle condition defines how the RI of the red Class IA/IB retro-reflector (P-05) is judged when its front surface gives a mirror effect.

candidates.text: In case the retro-reflector is not marked "TOP", its RI at the position of minimum RI (rotation about the axis of reference), at illumination angle β1 = β2 = 0° (or the angle specified in paragraph 5) and divergence angle 20', shall conform to the value specified in paragraph 5 (for red Class IA/IB: at least 300 mcd/lx).
candidates.test_case: Rotate the sample about its reference axis at α = 20', β1 = β2 = 0°, find the minimum-RI position and verify RI ≥ 300 mcd/lx.
candidates.applies_because: The R150 retro-reflector insert must meet its minimum RI in its least favourable rotational position if it carries no TOP marking.

candidates.text: In case the retro-reflector is not marked "TOP", the RI at the other angles of illumination and divergence shall meet the values of paragraph 5 with the device in the minimum-RI rotation position ε, with a permitted rotation of ±5° about the axis of reference from that position if the values are not attained.
candidates.test_case: Keep the device at the minimum-RI ε position (±5° allowed) and measure RI at all Table 3 angles for red Class IA/IB.
candidates.applies_because: This defines the rotation position at which the full photometric compliance of the non-TOP-marked retro-reflector is assessed.

candidates.text: In case the retro-reflector is marked "TOP", at illumination angle β1 = β2 = 0° and divergence angle 20', its RI shall not fall below the prescribed value (red Class IA/IB: 300 mcd/lx) in any position during a rotation of ±5° about its axis of reference.
candidates.test_case: Rotate the TOP-marked sample ±5° about its reference axis at α = 20', β1 = β2 = 0° and verify RI ≥ 300 mcd/lx throughout.
candidates.applies_because: A TOP-marked retro-reflector insert in the rear lamp must keep the minimum RI over a ±5° rotation.

candidates.text: If at β1 = β2 = 0° and ε = 0° the RI of the retro-reflector exceeds the specified value by 50 per cent or more, compliance at all angles of illumination and divergence shall be assessed at ε = 0°.
candidates.test_case: Measure RI at β1 = β2 = 0°, ε = 0°; if it is ≥ 150 % of the requirement, measure all Table 3 points at ε = 0° and verify the minimum values.
candidates.applies_because: This condition fixes the rotation position at which the retro-reflector's photometric compliance is judged.

candidates.text: The retro-reflection (RI) of the retro-reflector shall be assessed under illumination by CIE Standard Illuminant A (ISO 11664-2:2007(E)/CIE S 014-2/E:2006).
candidates.test_case: Verify in the photometric test report that the RI measurements were made with a CIE Standard Illuminant A source.
candidates.applies_because: The illuminant defines the conditions under which the RI limits for the retro-reflector apply.

candidates.text: The shape of the illuminating surfaces of the Class IA or IB retro-reflector shall not be easily confused with the triangular shape prescribed for trailer retro-reflectors (Classes IIIA/IIIB), when viewed from an observation distance of 10 metres.
candidates.test_case: Visually inspect the retro-reflector's illuminating surface from 10 m and confirm it cannot easily be confused with a triangle.
candidates.applies_because: The product's integral red retro-reflector is a non-triangular Class IA/IB device covered by Annex 5 paragraph 1.

candidates.text: For the water penetration test, the retro-reflector (whether part of the lamp or not), stripped of all removable parts, is immersed for 10 minutes in water at 50 °C ± 5 °C with the highest point of the upper part of the illuminating surface 20 mm below the water surface. The immersion is repeated with the device turned through 180°, so that the illuminating surface is at the bottom and the rear face is covered by about 20 mm of water. This applies to Class IA, and to Class IB unless the moisture and dust test of Annex 6 Part 3 is applied.
candidates.test_case: Immerse the stripped lamp/retro-reflector sample for 10 min at 50 ± 5 °C, face up and then face down, 20 mm below the water surface.
candidates.applies_because: The product's retro-reflector is Class IA or IB, part of a lamp, and is subject to the water penetration test.

candidates.text: Immediately after the 50 °C immersions, the retro-reflector sample is immersed under the same conditions in water at 25 °C ± 5 °C.
candidates.test_case: Transfer the sample immediately to a 25 ± 5 °C water bath and immerse it under the same conditions.
candidates.applies_because: This is the second-stage thermal shock exposure the Class IA/IB retro-reflector must withstand.

candidates.text: After the immersion test, no water shall penetrate to the reflecting surface of the retro-reflecting optical unit.
candidates.test_case: Visually inspect the reflecting (prism) surface for water after the immersion test.
candidates.applies_because: This is the pass criterion of the water penetration test for the product's retro-reflector.

candidates.text: If visual inspection clearly reveals the presence of water at the reflecting surface, the retro-reflector shall not be considered to have passed the water penetration test.
candidates.test_case: Record any visible water behind the lens or prisms as a test failure.
candidates.applies_because: Visible water ingress means the product's retro-reflector fails the test.

candidates.text: If visual inspection does not reveal water, or in case of doubt, the retro-reflector, after being lightly shaken to remove excess water from the outside, shall have a coefficient of luminous intensity (RI) that satisfies paragraph 5.1.4 when measured per paragraph 5.1.3.2.2. The measurement is made at an angle of divergence of 20' and an illumination angle of β1 = β2 = 0°, or if necessary in all positions of Annex 4 Part 1, paragraphs 1.1 and 1.2.
candidates.test_case: After shaking off water, measure RI at 20' divergence and β1 = β2 = 0° and compare it with the paragraph 5.1.4 limits for red Class IA/IB.
candidates.applies_because: This is the photometric pass criterion after the water penetration test for the product's retro-reflector.

candidates.text: In case of a Class IB retro-reflector (not watertight lamp) for which the manufacturer chooses the moisture and dust tests, the retro-reflector shall withstand a water spray with a precipitation rate at the device of 2.5 (+1.6/-0) mm/min.
candidates.test_case: Run the water spray cabinet test at a verified precipitation rate of 2.5 (+1.6/-0) mm/min on the mounted lamp.
candidates.applies_because: The open option of a non-watertight lamp makes the retro-reflector Class IB, and this moisture test is its alternative to the water penetration test.

candidates.text: In case of Class IB with moisture and dust tests, all drain holes and other openings of the lamp shall remain open during the water spray test, and any drain wicks used shall be tested in the device.
candidates.test_case: Inspect the test sample before spraying to confirm all drain holes and openings are open and drain wicks are fitted.
candidates.applies_because: This defines the lamp configuration exposed to moisture, so the drainage design of the combined lamp must cope with it.

candidates.text: In case of Class IB with moisture and dust tests, the rear position, stop and reversing lamp functions grouped or reciprocally incorporated with the retro-reflector shall be operated at design voltage during the water spray test in a cycle of 5 min ON and 55 min OFF.
candidates.test_case: Operate the lamp functions at design voltage with a 5 min ON / 55 min OFF cycle during the spray test and log the cycles.
candidates.applies_because: The retro-reflector is integrated in a rear combination lamp with signalling and lighting functions.

candidates.text: In case of Class IB with moisture and dust tests, the device shall be exposed to the water spray for 12 hours (12 cycles of 5/55 min).
candidates.test_case: Verify from the test log that the spray exposure lasted 12 hours over 12 cycles.
candidates.applies_because: This sets the moisture exposure duration that the lamp sealing and drainage must withstand.

candidates.text: In case of Class IB with moisture and dust tests, after the 1 hour drain period no standing pool of water shall be formed inside the device, nor be formable by tapping or tilting the device.
candidates.test_case: After draining, inspect the lamp interior, then tap and tilt the lamp and check that no standing pool of water forms.
candidates.applies_because: This is the pass criterion of the moisture test for the non-watertight lamp housing the retro-reflector.

candidates.text: In case of Class IB with moisture and dust tests, the RI of the retro-reflector measured after the water spray test according to Part 1 of Annex 4 shall satisfy the conditions of paragraph 5.1.4.
candidates.test_case: Measure RI at 20' divergence and β1 = β2 = 0° after the drain period and compare it with the paragraph 5.1.4 limits.
candidates.applies_because: The retro-reflector must keep its photometric performance after moisture exposure.

candidates.text: In case of Class IB with moisture and dust tests, the device shall be exposed to test dust of fine powdered cement in accordance with ASTM C 150-84, agitated at 15 min intervals for 2 to 15 s over a duration of 5 hours, with all drain holes and openings open.
candidates.test_case: Run the dust chamber test with ASTM C 150-84 cement for 5 hours with the prescribed agitation cycle.
candidates.applies_because: This defines the dust exposure that the non-watertight lamp containing the retro-reflector must resist.

candidates.text: In case of Class IB with moisture and dust tests, the RI of the retro-reflector measured after the dust exposure test according to paragraph 5.1.3.2.2 shall satisfy the conditions of paragraph 5.1.4.
candidates.test_case: After dust exposure and exterior cleaning, measure RI at 20' divergence and β1 = β2 = 0° and compare it with the paragraph 5.1.4 limits.
candidates.applies_because: Dust penetration must not significantly affect the photometric output of the retro-reflector.

candidates.text: The retro-reflector (Class IA/IB) shall be so designed that it retains the prescribed photometric and colorimetric characteristics despite the humidity and corrosive influences to which it is normally exposed.
candidates.test_case: After the saline mist corrosion test, check that the retro-reflector still meets its CIL and red night-time colour requirements.
candidates.applies_because: Annex 6 Part 4 is the corrosion resistance requirement applicable to the Class IA/IB retro-reflector built into the rear lamp.

candidates.text: The retro-reflector, or the complete rear lamp when the retro-reflector is combined with a lamp, shall withstand a saline mist exposure of 50 hours, with all removable parts stripped off. The exposure comprises two periods of 24 hours each, separated by a 2-hour interval in which the sample is allowed to dry.
candidates.test_case: Expose the lamp, stripped of removable parts, to salt spray per ISO 9227:2017 for 2 × 24 h with a 2 h drying interval, then assess it.
candidates.applies_because: The retro-reflector is combined with the rear position, stop and reversing lamps, so the whole lamp undergoes the corrosion exposure.

candidates.text: In case the retro-reflector has essential metal components susceptible to corrosion, the retro-reflector shall withstand a saline mist produced by atomizing, at 35 °C ± 2 °C, a solution of 5 parts by weight of sodium chloride in 95 parts of distilled water containing not more than 0.02 per cent of impurities.
candidates.test_case: Run the salt spray test at 35 °C ± 2 °C with a 5 % NaCl solution and verify the solution concentration and purity.
candidates.applies_because: Whether essential corrodible metal components (e.g. mirror-backed metallised prisms) are present is an open option for this retro-reflector.

candidates.text: Immediately after completion of the corrosion test, the retro-reflector sample shall not show signs of excessive corrosion liable to impair the efficiency of the device.
candidates.test_case: Visually inspect the retro-reflector front surface, rear face and metal components for corrosion or tarnishing immediately after the salt spray test.
candidates.applies_because: This pass criterion of the corrosion test applies to the Class IA/IB retro-reflector.

candidates.text: If the retro-reflector is mirror-backed (metallised prisms) with an accessible rear face, the accessible rear face of the moulded plastics Class IA or IB retro-reflector shall resist the rear-face test of Annex 6, Part 5.
candidates.test_case: Confirm by inspecting the design whether the retro-reflector is mirror-backed with an accessible rear face; if so, run the Annex 6 Part 5 rear-face test.
candidates.applies_because: The retro-reflector is a moulded PMMA Class IA/IB device, and the open option allows a mirror-backed design with an accessible rear face.

candidates.text: In case of a mirror-backed retro-reflector with accessible rear face, after the rear face has been brushed with a hard nylon brush, the rear face shall withstand the application for one minute of a cotton cloth soaked in the test mixture of 70 vol. per cent n-heptane and 30 vol. per cent toluol (Annex 7, Part 1).
candidates.test_case: Brush the rear face with a hard nylon brush, apply a cloth soaked in the 70/30 n-heptane/toluol mixture for 1 min, let it dry and brush again.
candidates.applies_because: This is the exposure prescribed for moulded plastics Class IA/IB retro-reflectors with a mirror-backed accessible rear face.

candidates.text: In case of a mirror-backed retro-reflector with accessible rear face, after the rear-face resistance test and with the whole mirror-backed rear face covered with Indian ink, the coefficient of luminous intensity (RI) measured at an angle of divergence of 20' and an illumination angle of β1 = β2 = 0° (or, if necessary, in all positions of Annex 4, Part 1, paragraphs 1.1 and 1.2) shall still satisfy the conditions of paragraph 5.1.4.
candidates.test_case: Cover the tested rear face fully with Indian ink, measure RI at 20' divergence and β1 = β2 = 0°, and compare the result with the paragraph 5.1.4 minimum values for red Class IA/IB.
candidates.applies_because: This pass criterion applies to Class IA/IB mirror-backed retro-reflectors after the rear-face test.

candidates.text: The outer surface of the retro-reflective device, in particular its illuminating surface, shall be resistant to a test mixture of 70 vol. per cent n-heptane and 30 vol. per cent toluol applied to it.
candidates.test_case: Lightly wipe the outer illuminating surface with a cotton cloth soaked in 70/30 n-heptane/toluol and inspect it.
candidates.applies_because: The Class IA/IB retro-reflector in the rear lamp must pass the R150 fuel resistance test.

candidates.text: About five minutes after the outer surface of the retro-reflective device has been wiped with the n-heptane/toluol test mixture, the surface must not show any apparent surface changes; slight surface cracks are not objected to.
candidates.test_case: About five minutes after wiping, visually inspect the illuminating surface for apparent changes other than slight surface cracks.
candidates.applies_because: This is the pass criterion of the fuel resistance test for the retro-reflective device (P-05, and the red outer lens where it covers the retro-reflector as a filter).

candidates.text: After the outer surface of the retro-reflective device, in particular the illuminating surface, has been exposed to a detergent lubricating oil for about 5 minutes and then cleaned, the coefficient of luminous intensity (CIL/RI) measured according to paragraph 5.1.3.2.2 shall satisfy the conditions of paragraph 5.1.4. The check is made at an angle of divergence of 20' and an illumination angle of β1 = β2 = 0°, or if necessary in all positions of Annex 4 Part 1 paras 1.1 and 1.2.
candidates.test_case: Wipe the illuminating surface of the retro-reflector sample with a cotton cloth soaked in detergent lubricating oil and leave it for 5 min, then clean it. Measure the CIL at 20' divergence and β1 = β2 = 0° and check it against the para 5.1.4 limits.
candidates.applies_because: The integral red Class IA/IB moulded plastics retro-reflector of the rear lamp falls under this lubricating-oil resistance test.

candidates.text: When the retro-reflector is marked following the Annex 10 single-device arrangements, the approval number must be placed close to the circle surrounding the letter "E", in any position relative to it.
candidates.test_case: Visually inspect the marking on the lamp sample and drawing to confirm that the approval number sits next to the E-circle.
candidates.applies_because: The Class IA/IB retro-reflector of the rear lamp carries an R150 approval mark.

candidates.text: The digits constituting the approval number must face the same way as the letter "E" of the approval mark.
candidates.test_case: Inspect the marking to confirm that the approval number digits have the same orientation as the "E".
candidates.applies_because: The retro-reflector's approval marking must follow this format.

candidates.text: The group of symbols indicating the class (IA or IB) must be diametrically opposite the approval number with respect to the circle surrounding the letter "E".
candidates.test_case: Inspect the marking to confirm that the class symbol is placed on the opposite side of the E-circle from the approval number.
candidates.applies_because: The Class IA or IB symbol is part of the retro-reflector's approval marking.

candidates.text: The external surface of the rear lamp as installed on the M1 vehicle (outer lens and any exposed housing rim/bezel or seal) shall not exhibit, directed outwards, any pointed or sharp parts.
candidates.test_case: Visually and tactilely inspect the installed lamp's exposed surfaces for outward-directed pointed or sharp parts.
candidates.applies_because: Para 2.3 counts lighting and light-signalling devices as part of the vehicle external surface.

candidates.text: The external surface of the rear lamp as installed shall not exhibit, directed outwards, any projections whose shape, dimensions, direction or hardness are likely to increase the risk or seriousness of bodily injury to a person hit by the external surface or brushing against it in the event of a collision.
candidates.test_case: Assess the projection shape, dimension, direction and hardness of the installed lamp, using the Annex 3 projection measurement methods.
candidates.applies_because: The lamp's exposed lens and rim form part of the M1 vehicle external surface.

candidates.text: The external surface of the rear lamp as installed shall not exhibit, directed outwards, any part likely to catch on pedestrians, cyclists or motor cyclists.
candidates.test_case: Inspect the installed lamp and its lens-to-body transitions for hook-like or catching features.
candidates.applies_because: The lamp's exposed surfaces form part of the vehicle external surface that may be contacted.

candidates.text: In case the lamp's outer lens, housing rim/bezel or seal protrudes beyond the surrounding panel by 5 mm or more, no protruding part of the lamp's external surface shall have a radius of curvature less than 2.5 mm.
candidates.test_case: Measure the projection per Annex 3 and the edge radii of the exposed lens and rim edges with radius gauges or a 3D scan.
candidates.applies_because: The protruding lamp edges are protruding parts of the external surface.

candidates.text: In case parts of the lamp's external surface protrude less than 5 mm but 1.5 mm or more, the outward-facing angles of those parts shall be blunted.
candidates.test_case: Measure the projection height per Annex 3 and inspect the outward-facing edges for blunting.
candidates.applies_because: This applies to the flush or slightly protruding lamp edges with radii below 2.5 mm.

candidates.text: In case a protruding part of the lamp's external surface (e.g. an exposed TPE/silicone seal) has a radius of curvature less than 2.5 mm and relies on the hardness exemption, that part shall be made of material with a hardness not exceeding 60 Shore A, measured with the component as installed on the vehicle.
candidates.test_case: Measure the Shore A hardness of the exposed part on the installed lamp, using a comparable method where Shore A is not possible.
candidates.applies_because: This applies to the open option of an exposed seal or edge with radius below 2.5 mm.

candidates.text: The rear lamp as installed on the approved M1 vehicle type shall be so manufactured in series production as to conform to the type approved, meeting the requirements of paragraphs 5 and 6. This covers the exposed outer lens, any exposed housing rim or bezel and any exposed seal: no outward-directed pointed or sharp parts or parts likely to catch, and a minimum radius of curvature of 2.5 mm, or the applicable projection-based or Shore A hardness exemptions.
candidates.test_case: Take random production lamps installed on the vehicle and check them against the approved type. Measure the edge radii and projections of the exposed lens, housing and seal with the Annex 3 methods, and measure the Shore A hardness of any exposed seal.
candidates.applies_because: The lamp's lens, and any exposed housing or seal, forms part of the M1 vehicle's external surface, so production parts must keep the external-projection properties of the approved type.

candidates.text: In case the rear lamp protrudes beyond the nominal line of the surrounding body panel and is mounted on a surface other than convex, so that its projection cannot be determined by simple measurement, the dimension of the lamp's projection shall be determined as the maximum variation of the distance of the centre of a 100 mm diameter sphere from the nominal line of the panel when the sphere is moved over the lamp while in constant contact with it.
candidates.test_case: Roll a 100 mm diameter sphere over the installed lamp and adjacent panel and record the maximum displacement of the sphere centre from the panel nominal line.
candidates.applies_because: The installed lamp is a component mounted on the vehicle's external surface, and its projection is assessed against the R26 projection limits using this method.

candidates.text: The lamp shall be fitted so that, under normal conditions of use and notwithstanding any vibrations to which it may be subjected, it retains the characteristics prescribed by this Regulation and enables the vehicle to comply with the requirements of this Regulation.
candidates.test_case: Vibration-test the installed lamp and its fasteners, then re-check its position, orientation and photometry on the vehicle.
candidates.applies_because: The rear combination lamp is a light-signalling device fitted to the M1 vehicle.

candidates.text: It shall not be possible for the lamp to be inadvertently maladjusted.
candidates.test_case: Inspect the mounting interface for positive location and check that the lamp cannot be shifted out of orientation by normal handling.
candidates.applies_because: The lamp's fasteners/clips must hold its aim on the vehicle.

candidates.text: When the lamp is fitted to the vehicle, the reference axis of each signalling function shall be parallel to the bearing plane of the vehicle on the road and parallel to the median longitudinal plane of the vehicle, with a tolerance of ±3° in each direction.
candidates.test_case: Measure the reference axis orientation of the installed lamp relative to the vehicle planes and check it is within ±3°.
candidates.applies_because: The rear position, stop and reversing lamps and the retro-reflector are signalling devices other than side devices.

candidates.text: Any specific fitting instructions laid down by the manufacturer of the lamp shall be complied with.
candidates.test_case: Compare the installation on the vehicle against the lamp manufacturer's fitting instructions.
candidates.applies_because: The lamp's installation must follow its manufacturer's fitting instructions.

candidates.text: In the absence of specific instructions, lamps constituting a pair (left and right rear combination lamps) shall be fitted to the vehicle symmetrically in relation to the median longitudinal plane, based on the exterior geometrical form of the lamp.
candidates.test_case: Measure the lateral positions of the left and right lamp exteriors relative to the vehicle centre plane.
candidates.applies_because: Rear position lamps, stop lamps and rear retro-reflectors are fitted as pairs on M1 vehicles.

candidates.text: Lamps constituting a pair shall be symmetrical to one another in relation to the median longitudinal plane; this does not apply to the interior structure of the lamp.
candidates.test_case: Compare the exterior geometry of the left-hand and right-hand lamps for mirror symmetry.
candidates.applies_because: The left and right rear combination lamps form a pair.

candidates.text: Lamps constituting a pair shall satisfy the same colorimetric requirements.
candidates.test_case: Measure the chromaticity of each function on the left and right lamps.
candidates.applies_because: The paired lamps emit red (position, stop, retro-reflector) and white (reversing) light.

candidates.text: Lamps constituting a pair shall have substantially identical photometric characteristics.
candidates.test_case: Compare the photometric test results of the left and right lamps for each function.
candidates.applies_because: The paired rear position, stop and retro-reflector functions must match left to right.

candidates.text: In case of a lamp incorporating a manufacturer logo, only two lateral logos (one on each side) or one central logo shall be fitted on the rear of the vehicle, and the logo shall be a vehicle manufacturer or body manufacturer logo.
candidates.test_case: Inspect the vehicle rear for the number and position of illuminated logos and check that each is a vehicle or body manufacturer logo.
candidates.applies_because: Open option: a logo may be integrated in the lens or light-emitting surface.

candidates.text: Where the rear position lamp, stop lamp, reversing lamp and retro-reflector are grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated, all requirements regarding colour, position, orientation, geometric visibility and electrical connections shall be fulfilled for each function.
candidates.test_case: Verify colour, position, orientation, geometric visibility and wiring for each function of the installed lamp.
candidates.applies_because: The product combines several functions in one lamp body.

candidates.text: The photometric and colorimetric requirements of each function shall be fulfilled when all other functions with which it is grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated are switched OFF.
candidates.test_case: Measure the photometry and colour of each function with all other functions switched OFF.
candidates.applies_because: The lamp groups or reciprocally incorporates several functions.

candidates.text: In case the rear position lamp is reciprocally incorporated with the stop lamp (or another function that can be switched ON together with it), the colour requirements of the stop lamp shall be fulfilled when both the stop lamp and the rear position lamp are switched ON.
candidates.test_case: Measure the stop lamp chromaticity with the stop and rear position functions ON simultaneously.
candidates.applies_because: Open option: the rear position lamp and stop lamp may be reciprocally incorporated.

candidates.text: In case a function of the lamp is a single lamp whose apparent surface is composed of two or more distinct parts, either the total projected area of the distinct parts in the direction of the reference axis shall occupy not less than 60 per cent of the smallest circumscribing quadrilateral, or the minimum distance between facing edges of adjacent distinct parts shall not exceed 75 mm measured perpendicular to the reference axis.
candidates.test_case: Project the apparent surface along the reference axis and compute the area ratio or measure the gap between parts.
candidates.applies_because: The LED/reflector-cell layout may create apparent surfaces composed of distinct parts.

candidates.text: In case the function is provided by an assembly of two lamps marked "D", either the projection of the apparent surfaces of the two lamps in the direction of the reference axis shall occupy not less than 60 per cent of the smallest circumscribing quadrilateral, or the minimum distance between their facing edges shall not exceed 75 mm measured perpendicular to the reference axis.
candidates.test_case: Measure the projected apparent surfaces of both 'D' lamps on the vehicle and compute the area ratio or edge gap.
candidates.applies_because: Open option: the lamp may be part of a 'D' lamp assembly.

candidates.text: In case the function is part of an interdependent lamp system marked "Y", the system shall fulfil the requirements of paragraph 5.7.2.1 (60 per cent area or 75 mm gap).
candidates.test_case: Measure the projected apparent surfaces of the interdependent lamps and check the 60 % or 75 mm criterion.
candidates.applies_because: Open option: the lamp may be part of an interdependent 'Y' system.

candidates.text: In the absence of specific instructions, the photometric characteristics (intensity, colour, apparent surface) of each lamp function shall not be intentionally varied while the lamp is switched ON.
candidates.test_case: Observe and measure each function over time while switched ON for unintended variation.
candidates.applies_because: Applies to the steady-burning rear position, stop and reversing lamps.

candidates.text: Red light emitted by the rear lamp shall not be visible from the front of the vehicle.
candidates.test_case: Check from the front of the vehicle that no red light from the lamp is visible.
candidates.applies_because: The lamp emits red light at the rear of the vehicle.

candidates.text: There shall be no direct visibility of the apparent surface of the red lamp to an observer moving within Zone 1 (between 1 m and 2.2 m above ground, bounded laterally by planes at 15° outward) in a transverse plane 25 m in front of the vehicle.
candidates.test_case: Perform a sight-line check from Zone 1 at 25 m in front of the vehicle per Annex 4.
candidates.applies_because: The lamp's red rear position and stop functions are red lamps at the rear.

candidates.text: In case of doubt, the luminous intensity of red light emitted to the front, as verified during lamp type approval, shall not exceed 0.25 cd per lamp, taking into account the influence of the vehicle body if applicable.
candidates.test_case: Measure the forward-emitted red intensity goniophotometrically and check it is ≤0.25 cd.
candidates.applies_because: This is the alternative criterion for red forward visibility of the rear lamp.

candidates.text: The electrical connections shall be such that the rear position lamps can only be switched ON and OFF simultaneously with the front position lamps and the rear registration plate lamp, except under the conditions of paragraph 5.11.1 (e.g. parking lamp use, daytime running lamps ON).
candidates.test_case: Operate the vehicle lighting switch and check that the rear position lamps switch together with the front position and plate lamps.
candidates.applies_because: The lamp contains the rear position lamp function.

candidates.text: In case the lamp is part of an interdependent lamp system, all light sources of the system shall be switched ON and OFF simultaneously.
candidates.test_case: Switch the function and verify that all interdependent lamps light and extinguish together.
candidates.applies_because: Open option: the lamp may be part of an interdependent 'Y' system.

candidates.text: The rear position lamp, stop lamp, reversing lamp and rear retro-reflector shall not be concealable.
candidates.test_case: Inspect the installation for any concealment device covering the lamp.
candidates.applies_because: Concealment is prohibited for all lamps other than headlamps and front fog lamps.

candidates.text: The colour of the light emitted by each lamp function shall be as specified in the colour table of paragraph 5.15.
candidates.test_case: Measure the chromaticity of each function and compare it with the specified colour.
candidates.applies_because: The lamp emits red and white signal light and contains a red retro-reflector.

candidates.text: Colours: reversing lamp – white; stop lamp – red; rear position lamp – red; rear retro-reflector, non-triangular – red.
candidates.test_case: Measure the chromaticity of each function against the white or red limits.
candidates.applies_because: These are the functions integrated in the rear combination lamp.

candidates.text: The number of lamps of each function mounted on the vehicle shall be equal to the number indicated in the individual specifications of this Regulation.
candidates.test_case: Count the installed functions on the vehicle and compare with paragraphs 6.4, 6.7, 6.10 and 6.14.
candidates.applies_because: The number of rear position, stop and reversing lamps and retro-reflectors installed is governed by section 6.

candidates.text: In case the rear position lamp or rear retro-reflector is installed on a movable component (e.g. tailgate), at all fixed positions of the movable component it shall meet all the position, geometric visibility, colorimetric and photometric requirements for that lamp.
candidates.test_case: Check position, visibility, colour and photometry with the movable component in each fixed position.
candidates.applies_because: The mounting location (fixed body or tailgate) is not settled by the profile.

candidates.text: The apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis of the rear position lamp and retro-reflector shall not be hidden more than 50 per cent by any movable component in any fixed position different from the normal position of use; otherwise additional lamps meeting all applicable requirements shall be switched ON.
candidates.test_case: Open each movable component to its fixed positions and measure the hidden share of the apparent surface.
candidates.applies_because: Movable components such as the tailgate may obscure the rear lamp.

candidates.text: In case the rear position lamp (category R2) and stop lamp (category S2) have variable luminous intensity control and are combined, grouped or reciprocally incorporated, their intensities shall vary all together in the same manner and in a similar proportion.
candidates.test_case: Vary the intensity-control inputs and measure both functions' intensities for proportional variation.
candidates.applies_because: Open option: the lamp may have variable intensity control.

candidates.text: In case of variable luminous intensity control, the prescribed ratio between the stop lamp and rear position lamp luminous intensities shall be maintained throughout variation transitions over the entire intensity range.
candidates.test_case: Record both intensities during transitions and verify the ratio over the whole range.
candidates.applies_because: Open option: the lamp may have variable intensity control.

candidates.text: In case of variable intensity control, a decrease of luminous intensity due to traffic conditions shall only be activated when the vehicle speed is ≤20 km/h or the distance to the following vehicle is ≤20 m, and it may only remain active as long as the speed is ≤50 km/h.
candidates.test_case: Drive or simulate speed and distance inputs and verify when the intensity decrease is activated and deactivated.
candidates.applies_because: Open option: the lamp may have variable intensity control.

candidates.text: In case of variable intensity control, no sharp variation of intensity shall be observed during transition.
candidates.test_case: Record the intensity versus time during transitions and check for steps.
candidates.applies_because: Open option: the lamp may have variable intensity control.

candidates.text: In case the lamp has no integrated electronic light source control gear or variable intensity control and was approved with a special power supply, secondary operating mode or applicant-requested voltage, the voltage supplied at the terminals of the stop lamp and rear position lamp shall not exceed the voltage specified for those functions as approved, with the vehicle electrical system in a constant voltage operating condition.
candidates.test_case: Measure the terminal voltage of the stop and rear position functions on the vehicle at constant system voltage.
candidates.applies_because: Open option: the electronic light source control gear may be external to the lamp.

candidates.text: In case the lamp has no integrated electronic light source control gear or variable intensity control and is not covered by paragraph 5.27.1, the voltage at the terminals of the stop lamp and rear position lamp shall not exceed 13.5 V (12 V system) by more than 3 per cent.
candidates.test_case: Measure the terminal voltage on the vehicle in constant voltage operating condition and check it is ≤13.9 V.
candidates.applies_because: Open option: the electronic light source control gear may be external to the lamp.

candidates.text: There shall be no obstacle inside the angles of geometric visibility to the propagation of light from any part of the apparent surface of the lamp observed from infinity, unless the obstacle was already present when the lamp was type-approved.
candidates.test_case: Check the geometric visibility angles of the installed lamp for obstruction by body parts.
candidates.applies_because: Each signalling function and the retro-reflector have prescribed geometric visibility angles.

candidates.text: If any part of the apparent surface of the installed lamp is hidden by further parts of the vehicle, the part of the lamp not hidden shall still conform to the photometric values prescribed for the approval of the device.
candidates.test_case: Measure photometry with the vehicle masking replicated and compare with the device approval values.
candidates.applies_because: Body panels may partly mask the rear combination lamp.

candidates.text: In case the lamp is part of an interdependent lamp system, the geometric visibility requirements shall be fulfilled when all its interdependent lamps are operated together.
candidates.test_case: Operate all interdependent lamps together and check the geometric visibility angles.
candidates.applies_because: Open option: the lamp may be part of an interdependent 'Y' system.

candidates.text: The rear position lamp, stop lamp and reversing lamp shall be type approved according to UN Regulation No. 148, and the rear retro-reflector according to UN Regulation No. 150, when installed on a vehicle.
candidates.test_case: Check the approval marks on the lamp and the R148/R150 approval documentation.
candidates.applies_because: The lamp functions and the retro-reflector require device approval for installation.

candidates.text: In case the lamp incorporates a manufacturer logo, the lamp shall be type approved according to UN Regulation No. 148.
candidates.test_case: Verify that the R148 approval covers the lamp configuration including the logo.
candidates.applies_because: Open option: a logo may be integrated in the lamp.

candidates.text: On M1 vehicles, one reversing lamp is mandatory and a second reversing lamp is optional.
candidates.test_case: Inspect the vehicle lighting layout and count the reversing lamps fitted.
candidates.applies_because: The lamp contains the reversing lamp function for an M1 passenger car.

candidates.text: The reversing lamp shall be type-approved according to the 00 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 23 or to the 00 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 148.
candidates.test_case: Check that the R148 (or R23) approval mark is present on the lamp and that the approval certificate is valid.
candidates.applies_because: The integrated reversing lamp must hold component approval to be installed.

candidates.text: The reversing lamp shall be installed not less than 250 mm and not more than 1,200 mm above the ground.
candidates.test_case: Measure the lowest and highest points of the reversing lamp apparent surface above the ground on the unladen vehicle.
candidates.applies_because: The lamp's position on the M1 body determines the height of the reversing lamp's apparent surface.

candidates.text: The reversing lamp shall be installed at the rear of the vehicle.
candidates.test_case: Inspect the installation location on the vehicle.
candidates.applies_because: The product is a rear-mounted reversing lamp.

candidates.text: The geometric visibility of a rear-mounted reversing lamp shall cover α = 15° upwards and 5° downwards.
candidates.test_case: Verify unobstructed visibility of the apparent surface at +15° and -5° vertical using CAD sight-line analysis or goniometric inspection on the vehicle.
candidates.applies_because: The apparent surface of the reversing lamp must remain visible within these vertical angles when installed.

candidates.text: In case of only one reversing lamp on the vehicle, the geometric visibility shall cover β = 45° to the right and to the left; in case of two reversing lamps, it shall cover β = 45° outwards and 30° inwards.
candidates.test_case: Check apparent surface visibility at the applicable horizontal angles by CAD or on-vehicle inspection.
candidates.applies_because: The horizontal visibility of the reversing lamp depends on whether one or two are fitted to the M1 vehicle.

candidates.text: The reversing lamp shall be oriented rearwards.
candidates.test_case: Verify that the reference axis of the installed lamp points rearwards, parallel to the vehicle longitudinal axis.
candidates.applies_because: The orientation of the reversing lamp's reference axis is set by the lamp design and its mounting.

candidates.text: The electrical connections of the reversing lamp shall be such that the lamp can be switched ON only if the reverse gear is engaged and the device which controls starting and stopping of the propulsion system is in a position in which operation of the propulsion system is possible.
candidates.test_case: Functional test on the vehicle: engage reverse gear with the propulsion system operable and check that the lamp switches ON.
candidates.applies_because: The wiring and control of the reversing lamp LED circuit must support this switching logic.

candidates.text: The reversing lamp shall not switch ON or remain ON if either the reverse gear is not engaged or the propulsion system is not in an operable state.
candidates.test_case: Functional test: disengage reverse gear and, separately, switch off the propulsion system, and check that the lamp is OFF in each case.
candidates.applies_because: The reversing lamp control must prevent operation outside the permitted conditions.
