candidates.text: A tell-tale indicating failure of the reversing lamp shall be provided if required by the component regulation.
candidates.test_case: Check R148 for failure-indication requirements and, if applicable, simulate an LED failure and verify that the tell-tale is activated.
candidates.applies_because: If R148 requires failure indication for the LED reversing lamp, the lamp must provide the failure signal.

candidates.text: Stop lamps of category S1 or S2 are mandatory on the vehicle.
candidates.test_case: Inspect the vehicle for the presence of S1/S2 stop lamps.
candidates.applies_because: The lamp contains the S1/S2 category stop lamp function for an M1 vehicle.

candidates.text: Two S1 or S2 category stop lamps shall be installed on the vehicle.
candidates.test_case: Count the S1/S2 stop lamps fitted to the vehicle.
candidates.applies_because: The rear combination lamp provides one of the two mandatory S1/S2 stop lamps.

candidates.text: The stop lamps shall be type-approved according to the 02 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 7 or to the 00 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 148.
candidates.test_case: Verify the R148 approval mark and certificate for the stop lamp function.
candidates.applies_because: The integrated stop lamp must hold component approval.

candidates.text: For M1 vehicles, the point on the apparent surface of an S1 or S2 stop lamp in the direction of the reference axis which is farthest from the vehicle's median longitudinal plane shall not be more than 400 mm from the extreme outer edge of the vehicle.
candidates.test_case: Measure the distance from the outer edge of the stop lamp apparent surface to the vehicle's extreme outer edge.
candidates.applies_because: The lateral position of the stop lamp's apparent surface within the lamp determines compliance on the M1 vehicle.

candidates.text: S1 or S2 stop lamps shall be installed not less than 350 mm nor more than 1,500 mm above the ground (2,100 mm if the shape of the bodywork makes it impossible to keep within 1,500 mm).
candidates.test_case: Measure the lowest and highest points of the stop lamp apparent surface above the ground.
candidates.applies_because: The height of the stop lamp's apparent surface is set by the lamp's position on the vehicle.

candidates.text: The horizontal plane tangential to the lower edge of the apparent surface of the S3 or S4 stop lamp shall be above the horizontal plane tangential to the upper edge of the apparent surface of the S1 or S2 stop lamps.
candidates.test_case: Measure the heights of the S1/S2 apparent surface upper edge and the S3/S4 apparent surface lower edge on the vehicle and compare them.
candidates.applies_because: The upper edge of the S1/S2 stop lamp in this rear lamp constrains the placement of the M1 vehicle's mandatory S3/S4 lamp.

candidates.text: S1 or S2 stop lamps shall be installed at the rear of the vehicle.
candidates.test_case: Inspect the installation location.
candidates.applies_because: The product is a rear lamp containing an S1/S2 stop lamp.

candidates.text: The geometric visibility of S1 or S2 stop lamps shall cover a horizontal angle of 45° to the left and to the right of the vehicle's longitudinal axis; where the lamp is mounted below 750 mm (measured from the H plane), the inward angle may be reduced to 20° under the H plane.
candidates.test_case: Check apparent surface visibility at 45° inward and outward (or 20° inward under the H plane if mounted below 750 mm) by CAD or on-vehicle inspection.
candidates.applies_because: The stop lamp's apparent surface and lamp contour must provide this horizontal visibility when installed.

candidates.text: The geometric visibility of S1 or S2 stop lamps shall cover a vertical angle of 15° above and below the horizontal; where the lamp is mounted below 750 mm (measured from the H plane), the downward angle may be reduced to 5°.
candidates.test_case: Check apparent surface visibility at +15° and -15° (or -5°) vertical by CAD or on-vehicle inspection.
candidates.applies_because: The stop lamp's apparent surface must be visible within these vertical angles when installed.

candidates.text: The stop lamp shall be oriented towards the rear of the vehicle.
candidates.test_case: Verify that the reference axis of the installed lamp points rearwards.
candidates.applies_because: The orientation of the stop lamp's reference axis is set by the lamp design and its mounting.

candidates.text: All stop lamps shall be switched ON simultaneously when the braking system provides the relevant signal defined in UN Regulations Nos. 13 and 13-H.
candidates.test_case: Apply the service brake and verify that all stop lamps illuminate simultaneously.
candidates.applies_because: The stop lamp LED circuit must respond to the vehicle braking signal.

candidates.text: A tell-tale indicating failure of the stop lamp shall be provided if required by the component regulation.
candidates.test_case: If required by R148, simulate an LED failure and verify that the failure tell-tale is activated.
candidates.applies_because: If R148 requires failure indication for the LED stop lamp, the lamp must provide the failure signal.

candidates.text: Rear position lamps of category R, R1 or R2 are mandatory on the vehicle.
candidates.test_case: Inspect the vehicle for the presence of rear position lamps.
candidates.applies_because: The lamp contains the rear position lamp function.

candidates.text: Two rear position lamps shall be installed, type-approved according to the 02 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 7 or to the 00 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 148.
candidates.test_case: Verify the R148 approval mark on the lamp and count the rear position lamps on the vehicle.
candidates.applies_because: The integrated rear position lamp must hold component approval and is one of the two mandatory lamps.

candidates.text: The point on the apparent surface of the rear position lamp in the direction of the reference axis which is farthest from the vehicle's median longitudinal plane shall not be more than 400 mm from the extreme outer edge of the vehicle.
candidates.test_case: Measure the distance from the outer edge of the apparent surface to the vehicle's extreme outer edge.
candidates.applies_because: The lateral position of the rear position lamp's apparent surface within the lamp determines compliance.

candidates.text: Rear position lamps shall be installed not less than 350 mm nor more than 1,500 mm above the ground (2,100 mm if the shape of the bodywork makes it impossible to keep within 1,500 mm).
candidates.test_case: Measure the lowest and highest points of the apparent surface above the ground.
candidates.applies_because: The height of the rear position lamp's apparent surface is set by the lamp's position on the vehicle.

candidates.text: Rear position lamps shall be installed at the rear of the vehicle.
candidates.test_case: Inspect the installation location.
candidates.applies_because: The product is a rear lamp.

candidates.text: The geometric visibility of the rear position lamp shall cover a horizontal angle of 45° inwards and 80° outwards; where the lamp is mounted below 750 mm (measured from the H plane), the inward angle may be reduced to 20° under the H plane.
candidates.test_case: Check apparent surface visibility at 45° inward (or 20°) and 80° outward by CAD sight-line analysis or on-vehicle inspection.
candidates.applies_because: The 80° outward visibility drives the wrap-around design of the rear position lamp's apparent surface.

candidates.text: The geometric visibility of the rear position lamp shall cover a vertical angle of 15° above and below the horizontal; where the lamp is mounted below 750 mm (measured from the H plane), the downward angle may be reduced to 5°.
candidates.test_case: Check visibility at +15° and -15° (or -5°) vertical.
candidates.applies_because: The rear position lamp's apparent surface must be visible within these vertical angles when installed.

candidates.text: In case of the M1 alternative where a rear side-marker lamp is installed, the geometric visibility of the rear position lamp shall cover a horizontal angle of 45° outwards to 45° inwards (inward angle reducible to 20° under the H plane if mounted below 750 mm) and a vertical angle of 15° above and below the horizontal (downward angle reducible to 5° if mounted below 750 mm).
candidates.test_case: If this alternative is used, confirm a rear side-marker lamp is fitted and check visibility at the reduced angles.
candidates.applies_because: The manufacturer may use this alternative visibility option for M1 vehicles fitted with a rear side-marker lamp.

candidates.text: In case the alternative of paragraph 6.10.5.2 is applied, the rear position lamp shall provide an unobstructed view of at least 12.5 cm² of apparent surface at each visibility angle, excluding the illuminating surface of any retro-reflector that does not transmit light.
candidates.test_case: Compute the projected unobstructed apparent surface area, excluding the retro-reflector, at the boundary angles and confirm it is at least 12.5 cm².
candidates.applies_because: The integral retro-reflector must not be counted towards the visible apparent surface of the rear position lamp.

candidates.text: The rear position lamp shall be oriented rearwards.
candidates.test_case: Verify that the reference axis of the installed lamp points rearwards.
candidates.applies_because: The orientation of the rear position lamp's reference axis is set by the lamp design and its mounting.

candidates.text: The electrical connections of the rear position lamps shall be such that they are switched ON and OFF simultaneously with the front position lamps, the end-outline and side-marker lamps (if fitted) and the rear registration plate lamp, except in the cases listed in paragraph 5.11.1.
candidates.test_case: Switch the position lamps ON and OFF and verify that all the listed lamps change state simultaneously.
candidates.applies_because: The rear position lamp LED circuit must be wired per paragraph 5.11.

candidates.text: A closed-circuit tell-tale, combined with that of the front position lamps, shall be provided for the rear position lamps, and a tell-tale indicating failure shall be provided if required by the component regulation.
candidates.test_case: Switch the position lamps ON and verify that the tell-tale lights; if R148 requires it, simulate an LED failure and verify the failure indication.
candidates.applies_because: The rear position lamp operation and any R148 failure signal must be indicated to the driver.

candidates.text: Rear non-triangular retro-reflectors are mandatory on motor vehicles.
candidates.test_case: Inspect the vehicle for rear retro-reflectors.
candidates.applies_because: The lamp integrates the rear non-triangular retro-reflector for an M1 motor vehicle.

candidates.text: Two rear non-triangular retro-reflectors shall be installed, type-approved as Class IA or IB retro-reflectors according to the 02 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 3 or to the 00 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 150.
candidates.test_case: Verify the R150 Class IA or IB approval mark on the retro-reflector and count the units on the vehicle.
candidates.applies_because: The integral retro-reflector, whether Class IA (watertight lamp) or Class IB, must hold R150/R3 approval.

candidates.text: Any additional retro-reflecting devices and materials shall not impair the effectiveness of the mandatory lighting and light-signalling devices.
candidates.test_case: Inspect the lamp for additional retro-reflective elements and assess their effect on the mandatory functions.
candidates.applies_because: Any further retro-reflective elements in the lamp must not degrade the signal functions.

candidates.text: The point on the illuminating surface of the rear retro-reflector which is farthest from the vehicle's median longitudinal plane shall not be more than 400 mm from the extreme outer edge of the vehicle.
candidates.test_case: Measure the distance from the outer edge of the retro-reflector illuminating surface to the vehicle's extreme outer edge.
candidates.applies_because: The lateral position of the retro-reflector within the lamp determines compliance.

candidates.text: The rear retro-reflector shall be installed not less than 250 mm and, when grouped with rear lamps, not more than 1,200 mm above the ground (1,500 mm if the shape of the bodywork makes it impossible to keep within 1,200 mm).
candidates.test_case: Measure the lowest and highest points of the retro-reflector illuminating surface above the ground.
candidates.applies_because: The retro-reflector is grouped with the rear lamps in this lamp body.

candidates.text: The rear retro-reflector shall be installed at the rear of the vehicle.
candidates.test_case: Inspect the installation location.
candidates.applies_because: The retro-reflector is part of the rear lamp.

candidates.text: The geometric visibility of the rear retro-reflector shall cover a horizontal angle of 30° inwards and outwards.
candidates.test_case: Check visibility of the retro-reflector illuminating surface at ±30° horizontal by CAD or on-vehicle inspection.
candidates.applies_because: The retro-reflector insert and the lens contour must not obstruct visibility within this angle.

candidates.text: The geometric visibility of the rear retro-reflector shall cover a vertical angle of 10° above and below the horizontal; where the retro-reflector is mounted below 750 mm (measured from the H plane), the downward angle may be reduced to 5°.
candidates.test_case: Check visibility at +10° and -10° (or -5°) vertical.
candidates.applies_because: The retro-reflector must be visible within these vertical angles when installed.

candidates.text: The rear retro-reflector shall be oriented rearwards.
candidates.test_case: Verify that the reference axis of the retro-reflector points rearwards when installed.
candidates.applies_because: The orientation of the retro-reflector's reference axis is set by the lamp design and its mounting.

candidates.text: When the stop lamps are used for the emergency stop signal, the emergency stop signal shall be given by the simultaneous operation of all the stop lamps fitted, including the stop lamp function of this rear combination lamp.
candidates.test_case: On the vehicle, trigger the emergency braking logic signal and check that all stop lamps, including this lamp, operate simultaneously.
candidates.applies_because: The lamp's stop lamp function is mandatory on M1 vehicles and is one of the lamps that may give the emergency stop signal.

candidates.text: When used for the emergency stop signal, the LED stop lamp shall flash in phase with all other emergency stop signal lamps at a frequency of 4.0 ± 1.0 Hz.
candidates.test_case: Record the stop lamp light output with a photodiode during emergency stop signal activation and verify the flash frequency is 3.0–5.0 Hz and in phase with the other lamps.
candidates.applies_because: The LED stop lamp and its driver must be able to flash at the emergency stop signal frequency.

candidates.text: When the stop lamp gives the emergency stop signal, its geometric visibility shall be as specified for the S1/S2 stop lamp in paragraph 6.7.5: 45° to the left and right horizontally (inward angle reducible to 20° under the H plane if mounted below 750 mm) and 15° above and below the horizontal (downward angle reducible to 5° if mounted below 750 mm).
candidates.test_case: Verify the visible apparent surface of the stop lamp over the prescribed angular field on the installed lamp or a CAD visibility study.
candidates.applies_because: The emergency stop signal uses the stop lamp function of this lamp at its installed position.

candidates.text: The stop lamp function of the rear combination lamp shall not be used to provide the answer-back signal.
candidates.test_case: Inspect the vehicle wiring and control logic to confirm that the stop lamp is not activated on lock or unlock.
candidates.applies_because: Stop lamps are explicitly excluded from answer-back signal use, and this lamp contains a stop lamp.

candidates.text: In case the rear position lamp or reversing lamp of this device is used for the answer-back signal, the maximum luminous intensity of that lamp shall not exceed 700 cd on or above the HH line.
candidates.test_case: Goniophotometer measurement of the lamp in its answer-back mode, checking the maximum intensity at and above HH is ≤ 700 cd.
candidates.applies_because: The rear position or reversing lamp may be used as an answer-back signal lamp.

candidates.text: In case the rear position lamp or reversing lamp of this device is used for a flashing answer-back signal, the flash frequency shall not exceed 2.0 Hz.
candidates.test_case: Measure the flash frequency of the answer-back signal with a photodiode and oscilloscope.
candidates.applies_because: The lamp's LED electronics may drive a flashing answer-back signal.

candidates.text: In case a lamp of this device is used for the answer-back signal, the duration of the optical indication shall not exceed 3 seconds from the beginning to the end of the signal, irrespective of flashes, intensity variations or apparent surface variations.
candidates.test_case: Time the answer-back light output from start to end on lock and unlock events.
candidates.applies_because: The rear position or reversing lamp may provide the answer-back signal.

candidates.text: In case the rear position lamp is designed for the reduced geometric visibility of paragraph 6.10.5.2 on an M1 vehicle less than 6 m in length, side-marker lamps shall be used to supplement the reduced geometric visibility of the rear position lamp.
candidates.test_case: Check the visibility design option of the rear position lamp and confirm that rear side-marker lamps are fitted on the vehicle where 6.10.5.2 is used.
candidates.applies_because: The rear position lamp may take the M1 alternative reduced-visibility option, which requires side-marker lamps on the vehicle.

candidates.text: Any vehicle approved pursuant to this Regulation shall be so manufactured as to conform to the type approved by meeting the requirements set out in paragraphs 5. and 6. In particular, the production rear combination lamps (rear position, stop and reversing lamps and rear retro-reflector) as fitted shall keep the installation, visibility, colour and intensity characteristics of the approved vehicle type.
candidates.test_case: Take random production vehicles fitted with the lamp and repeat the Annex 9 checks (presence, colour, position, geometric visibility and light intensity of each function) against the approved type.
candidates.applies_because: Production lamps fitted to the approved M1 vehicle must continue to enable compliance with paras 5 and 6 under the CoP checks.

candidates.text: In the case where the non-textured outer lens is excluded and the apparent surface of a function (F2) is determined according to paragraph 2.10.2 as in example 7b, the adjacent function F1 shall not be transparent to F2.
candidates.test_case: Inspect the drawing and the lit sample to confirm that the optical parts of F1 do not transmit light emitted by F2 within the declared apparent surface.
candidates.applies_because: The rear combination lamp has adjacent red functions (rear position, stop) behind a common outer lens, so the apparent surface of one function may be bounded by another.

candidates.text: There shall be no direct visibility of the apparent surface of the red rear position lamp or red stop lamp of the rear combination lamp when viewed by an observer moving within Zone 1 (Annex 4) in a transverse plane situated 25 m in front of the vehicle.
candidates.test_case: With the lamp installed on the vehicle, sweep the observation point across Zone 1 at 25 m in front of the vehicle and confirm, by inspection or CAD sight-line analysis, that no red apparent surface is visible.
candidates.applies_because: The lamp emits red light (rear position and stop functions), so its installed apparent surfaces must not be visible from the front.

candidates.text: For the front-visibility check of red light, Zone 1 is bounded in height by two horizontal planes 1 m and 2.2 m above the ground. In width it is bounded by two vertical planes that form an angle of 15° outwards to the front from the vehicle's median longitudinal plane. These planes pass through the foremost point(s) of contact of the vertical planes parallel to the median longitudinal plane that delimit the vehicle's overall width.
candidates.test_case: Construct Zone 1 (1 m to 2.2 m height, 15° outward planes through the foremost overall-width points) in the vehicle CAD model and check the sight lines to the lamp's red apparent surfaces.
candidates.applies_because: This zone defines the observation region in which the red apparent surfaces of the rear lamp must not be directly visible.

candidates.text: In case of doubt, the requirement of no red light visibility towards the front shall be deemed fulfilled if the luminous intensity of red light emitted to the front, as verified during type approval of the lamp, is not more than 0.25 cd per lamp, taking into account the influence of the vehicle body if applicable.
candidates.test_case: Measure on a goniophotometer the red luminous intensity emitted into the forward directions covered by Zone 1, with the vehicle body influence included if applicable, and verify it is ≤ 0.25 cd per lamp.
candidates.applies_because: This alternative criterion applies to the red rear position and stop functions of the lamp when direct visibility towards the front is in doubt.

candidates.text: On production vehicles, the measured width, height and length positions of the rear position lamp, stop lamp, reversing lamp and rear retro-reflector, checked per paragraphs 2.10.2, 2.10.3, 2.10.4, 2.3.3 and 5.4, shall be such that the individual specifications applicable to each lamp are fulfilled.
candidates.test_case: Measure the illuminating-surface edges of each function on an unladen production vehicle and compare them with the width, height and length limits of paras 6.4, 6.7, 6.10 and 6.14.
candidates.applies_because: The lamp's illuminating surfaces set the installed positions checked in conformity of production for the M1 vehicle.

candidates.text: On production vehicles, the measured angles of geometric visibility of each lamp function, checked per paragraph 2.10.7, shall fulfil the individual specifications applicable to each lamp, with an allowance on the angle limits of no more than the ±3° permitted in paragraph 5.3 for mounting.
candidates.test_case: Check visibility of each function's apparent surface over the required horizontal and vertical angles on the production vehicle, allowing ±3° on the limits.
candidates.applies_because: The lamp's apparent surfaces and mounting determine the geometric visibility checked on production vehicles.

candidates.text: On production vehicles, the visibility of red light towards the front and of white light towards the rear shall comply with paragraph 5.10.
candidates.test_case: Check visibility from Zone 1 at 25 m in front of the vehicle and from Zone 2 at 25 m behind the vehicle per Annex 4.
candidates.applies_because: The lamp emits red light at the rear and white reversing light, so the confusion-light provisions are checked.

candidates.text: Red light emitted by the rear position lamp, stop lamp and red retro-reflector fitted on the rear of the vehicle shall not be visible from the front of the vehicle.
candidates.test_case: Observer moving within Zone 1 in a transverse plane 25 m in front of the vehicle confirms there is no direct view of the red apparent surface.
candidates.applies_because: The product is a red rear lamp fitted on the rear of an M1 vehicle.

candidates.text: In case of doubt, the luminous intensity of red light emitted towards the front by the lamp, as verified at lamp type approval, shall not exceed 0.25 cd per lamp, taking into account the influence of the vehicle body if applicable.
candidates.test_case: Measure the forward-directed red luminous intensity of the lamp on a goniophotometer and confirm it is ≤0.25 cd.
candidates.applies_because: This is the fallback criterion for the product's red rear functions.

candidates.text: When every lamp supplied by the vehicle electrical system is switched on, the rear position lamp, stop lamp and reversing lamp and their tell-tales shall function in accordance with paragraphs 5.11 to 5.14 and with the individual specifications applicable to each lamp.
candidates.test_case: Switch on each function on the production vehicle and verify correct activation, switching logic and tell-tale operation.
candidates.applies_because: The LED functions of the lamp are supplied by the vehicle electrical system and are checked in production.

candidates.text: The presence, number, colour (red for the rear position lamp, stop lamp and retro-reflector; white for the reversing lamp), arrangement and, where applicable, category of the lamps shall meet paragraphs 5.15 and 5.16 and the individual specifications applicable to each lamp.
candidates.test_case: Visually inspect the lamp's functions, colours and approval markings on the production vehicle against paras 5.15, 5.16 and 6.x.
candidates.applies_because: The lamp provides red and white rear functions whose colour, number and category are checked visually on production vehicles.

candidates.text: The markings on the lamps shall allow the presence, number, colour, arrangement and category of the lamps to be verified by visual inspection.
candidates.test_case: Inspect the lamp for legible approval markings that identify each function and category.
candidates.applies_because: The lamp's approval markings (R148/R150) are used for this production check.

rejected.text: The moulded plastics retro-reflector (Class IA or IB) shall be subjected to heat exposure for 48 consecutive hours in a dry atmosphere at a temperature of 65 °C ± 2 °C, followed by cooling for 1 hour at 23 °C ± 2 °C.
rejected.applies_because: The PMMA moulded-prism retro-reflector is a Class IA/IB moulded plastics reflector covered by this heat resistance test.
rejected.test_case: Condition the retro-reflector samples in a dry oven at 65 °C ± 2 °C for 48 h, then cool for 1 h at 23 °C ± 2 °C before inspection.

rejected.text: After the heat resistance test, no cracking or appreciable distortion of the retro-reflective device, and in particular of its optical component, must be visible.
rejected.applies_because: This is the pass criterion of the heat test that applies to the Class IA/IB retro-reflector.
rejected.test_case: Visually inspect the heat-conditioned retro-reflector and its prism optics for cracks or appreciable distortion.
